title: When to Trust Whom: A Context-Aware Graph Routing Mechanism for Information Diffusion Prediction

problem.claim: Information diffusion prediction forecasts future cascade participants from an observed cascade prefix.

gap.claim: Existing learn-then-fuse models combine social-graph and cascade-interaction views despite systematic mismatch, which can make static fusion ill-posed and cause negative interference.

contributions.claim: CARD is a context-aware routing framework that performs step-wise evidence arbitration between graph-derived views.
CARD uses social, interaction, consensus, and graph-agnostic prior experts in an expert pool.
CARD's router hard-selects the single most reliable expert at each decoding step.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets reportedly show state-of-the-art accuracy and stronger robustness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Information diffusion prediction supports proactive intervention by forecasting future participants from an observed cascade prefix.
Existing models encode social and interaction graphs and combine them through gated fusion before sequential decoding.
The two graph views are systematically mismatched, making static fusion vulnerable to compromise and negative interference.
View reliability depends on consensus, cold-start conditions, and cascade stage.
CARD routes decoding through selected experts and is reported to achieve strong accuracy and robustness across four real-world datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported accuracy or robustness.
The abstract does not detail the router's training objective or selection criteria.
